purpose: P0-S2 evidence batch 2b: IS-study, IS-work, PL-study, PL-work, MT-study, MT-work, CZ-study, CZ-work.

records.claim: Third-country nationals wishing to study in Iceland must obtain a residence permit for study purposes. Applicants must be accepted at a recognised Icelandic educational institution, demonstrate sufficient financial means, hold valid health insurance, and satisfy the general conditions for entry and residence under Icelandic immigration law.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Directorate of Immigration Iceland guidance for study residence permits.

records.claim: Iceland requires study-permit applicants to demonstrate sufficient financial means to cover living costs and tuition for the duration of their studies. Applicants must show they can support themselves without recourse to public funds; the applicable threshold is assessed against current Icelandic subsistence reference amounts.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Directorate of Immigration Iceland financial-means requirements for study permits.

records.claim: Applications for an Icelandic study residence permit are submitted to the Directorate of Immigration. Applicants outside Iceland apply at the Icelandic consulate or embassy in their country of residence. The permit is issued for the duration of the study programme and must be renewed annually with proof of continued enrolment.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Directorate of Immigration Iceland application process for study permits.

records.claim: Third-country nationals seeking employment in Iceland must obtain a work and residence permit. The applicant must have a confirmed job offer from an Icelandic employer. The employer must demonstrate that the position could not be filled by an Icelandic or EEA national, subject to the applicable labour-market test, unless the occupation is on the shortage list.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Directorate of Immigration Iceland guidance for work and residence permits.

records.claim: Iceland's work residence permit requires the applicant to receive remuneration in accordance with the applicable Icelandic collective agreement or statutory minimum for the role and sector. The salary must be specified in the employment contract and comply with Icelandic labour law.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Directorate of Immigration Iceland financial requirements for work permits.

records.claim: Applications for an Icelandic work and residence permit are submitted to the Directorate of Immigration. The employer typically initiates the application. Applicants outside Iceland apply at the Icelandic consulate or embassy. The permit is tied to the specific employer and must be renewed if employment changes.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Directorate of Immigration Iceland application process for work permits.

records.claim: Third-country nationals wishing to study in Poland must obtain a temporary residence permit for the purpose of study. Applicants must hold a valid acceptance or enrolment letter from a Polish higher-education institution, demonstrate sufficient financial means, hold valid health insurance, and satisfy the general conditions for entry and residence under Polish immigration law.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Office for Foreigners Poland guidance for temporary residence permit for study.

records.claim: Poland requires study-permit applicants to demonstrate stable and regular financial means sufficient to cover living costs and tuition. The applicable subsistence threshold is set by Polish law; applicants must show they can support themselves without recourse to public funds for the duration of the permit.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Office for Foreigners Poland financial-means requirements for study permits.

records.claim: Applications for a Polish study temporary residence permit are submitted to the voivode (regional governor) competent for the applicant's place of residence in Poland. Applicants outside Poland apply at the Polish consulate for a national visa, then apply for the residence permit after arrival. The permit is issued for up to 15 months and must be renewed.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Office for Foreigners Poland application process for study permits.

records.claim: Third-country nationals seeking employment in Poland must obtain a temporary residence and work permit. The applicant must have a valid employment contract or job offer from a Polish employer. The employer must obtain a work permit or declaration of intent to entrust work before the residence permit application is submitted.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Office for Foreigners Poland guidance for temporary residence and work permit.

records.claim: Poland's work residence permit requires the applicant to receive remuneration at least equal to the applicable Polish minimum wage for the role. The salary must be specified in the employment contract and comply with Polish labour law; the minimum wage is updated annually.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Office for Foreigners Poland financial requirements for work permits.

records.claim: Applications for a Polish temporary residence and work permit are submitted to the voivode competent for the applicant's place of residence in Poland. The employer must first obtain a work permit or declaration; the applicant then applies for the combined residence and work permit. The permit is tied to the specific employer and role.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Office for Foreigners Poland application process for work permits.

records.claim: Third-country nationals wishing to study in Malta must obtain a residence permit for study purposes. Applicants must hold a valid acceptance letter from a recognised Maltese educational institution, demonstrate sufficient financial means, hold valid health insurance, and satisfy the general conditions for entry and residence under Maltese immigration law.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Identità Malta guidance for study residence permits.

records.claim: Malta requires study-permit applicants to demonstrate sufficient financial means to cover tuition fees and living costs for the duration of their studies. Applicants must show they can support themselves without recourse to public funds; the applicable threshold is assessed against current Maltese subsistence reference amounts.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Identità Malta financial-means requirements for study permits.

records.claim: Applications for a Maltese study residence permit are submitted to Identità Malta. Applicants outside Malta apply at the Maltese consulate or embassy in their country of residence. The permit is issued for the duration of the study programme and must be renewed annually with proof of continued enrolment.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Identità Malta application process for study permits.

records.claim: Third-country nationals seeking employment in Malta must obtain a Single Permit combining residence and work authorisation. The applicant must have a confirmed job offer from a Maltese employer. The employer must demonstrate that the position could not be filled by a Maltese or EU/EEA national, subject to the applicable labour-market test.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Identità Malta Single Permit guidance.

records.claim: Malta's Single Permit requires the applicant to receive remuneration at least equal to the applicable Maltese minimum wage or the sector-specific rate for the role. The salary must be specified in the employment contract and comply with Maltese labour law.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Identità Malta Single Permit financial requirements.

records.claim: Applications for a Maltese Single Permit are submitted to Identità Malta. The employer initiates the application on behalf of the applicant. Applicants outside Malta apply at the Maltese consulate or embassy. The permit is tied to the specific employer and role and must be renewed if employment changes.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Identità Malta Single Permit application process.

records.claim: Third-country nationals wishing to study in Czechia must obtain a long-term residence permit for the purpose of study. Applicants must hold a valid acceptance letter from a recognised Czech higher-education institution, demonstrate sufficient financial means, hold valid health insurance, and satisfy the general conditions for entry and residence under Czech immigration law.
records.sourceAuthority: Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic
records.methodology: Direct review of current Ministry of the Interior Czech Republic guidance for long-term residence permit for study.

records.claim: Czechia requires study-permit applicants to demonstrate sufficient financial means to cover living costs and tuition. The applicable subsistence threshold is set by Czech law; applicants must show they can support themselves without recourse to public funds for the duration of the permit.
records.sourceAuthority: Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic
records.methodology: Direct review of current Ministry of the Interior Czech Republic financial-means requirements for study permits.

records.claim: Applications for a Czech long-term residence permit for study are submitted at the Czech consulate or embassy in the applicant's country of residence before arrival. After arrival, the applicant must register with the Ministry of the Interior. The permit is issued for the duration of the study programme and must be renewed annually.
records.sourceAuthority: Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic
records.methodology: Direct review of current Ministry of the Interior Czech Republic application process for study permits.

records.claim: Third-country nationals seeking employment in Czechia must obtain an Employee Card combining long-term residence and work authorisation. The applicant must have a confirmed job offer from a Czech employer for a position listed in the central register of job vacancies for Employee Card holders.
records.sourceAuthority: Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic
records.methodology: Direct review of current Ministry of the Interior Czech Republic Employee Card guidance.

records.claim: Czechia's Employee Card requires the applicant to receive remuneration at least equal to the applicable Czech minimum wage or the guaranteed wage for the relevant job category. The salary must be specified in the employment contract and comply with Czech labour law.
records.sourceAuthority: Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic
records.methodology: Direct review of current Ministry of the Interior Czech Republic Employee Card financial requirements.

records.claim: Applications for a Czech Employee Card are submitted at the Czech consulate or embassy in the applicant's country of residence. The employer must first list the vacancy in the central register; the applicant then applies for the Employee Card with the job offer and supporting documents. The card is tied to the specific employer and role.
records.sourceAuthority: Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic
records.methodology: Direct review of current Ministry of the Interior Czech Republic Employee Card application process.
